parts.name: cornea
parts.summary: The clear front window of the eye; does most of the focusing
parts.details: Transparent, avascular dome providing about two-thirds of the eye's refractive power (about 43 dioptres). Its focusing power is fixed.
parts.safety: Very sensitive; scratches (corneal abrasions) are common and painful.

parts.name: aqueous humour
parts.summary: Clear fluid that fills the front of the eye
parts.details: Made by the ciliary body, it flows through the pupil and drains at the angle via the trabecular meshwork; it nourishes the lens and cornea and sets intraocular pressure.
parts.safety: If drainage is blocked, pressure rises: that's glaucoma, which can damage the optic nerve.

parts.name: iris and pupil
parts.summary: The coloured ring; changes the pupil size to control light
parts.details: The sphincter pupillae (parasympathetic) constricts the pupil; the dilator pupillae (sympathetic) widens it.
parts.safety: Unequal or unreactive pupils can be a sign of a serious problem.

parts.name: crystalline lens
parts.details: Accommodation: for near vision the ciliary muscle contracts, the zonular fibres slacken and the elastic lens becomes rounder and more powerful.
parts.safety: Clouding of the lens with age is a cataract; stiffening with age is presbyopia.

parts.name: ciliary body and zonules
parts.summary: A ring of muscle that pulls on the lens to focus
parts.details: The ciliary muscle (parasympathetic, CN III) controls zonular tension; the ciliary processes secrete aqueous humour.

parts.name: vitreous humour
parts.summary: Clear jelly that fills most of the eyeball
parts.details: Gel of water, collagen and hyaluronic acid that keeps the eye's shape and transmits light to the retina.
parts.safety: New floaters with flashes need urgent review: possible retinal tear.

parts.name: retina and macula
parts.summary: The light-sensing layer at the back, like a camera sensor
parts.details: Rods (dim light) and cones (colour, detail) turn light into signals. The fovea at the centre of the macula is packed with cones for sharp central vision.
parts.safety: A curtain or shadow over vision can be retinal detachment: an emergency.

parts.name: choroid
parts.summary: A layer of blood vessels that feeds the retina
parts.details: Highly vascular layer supplying the outer retina, including the photoreceptors.

parts.name: sclera
parts.details: Dense collagen that protects the eye and anchors the six extraocular muscles; continuous with the cornea at the limbus.

parts.name: optic nerve
parts.summary: The cable that carries the picture to the brain
parts.details: Cranial nerve II, made of retinal ganglion cell axons. Where it leaves the eye (the optic disc) there are no photoreceptors: the blind spot.

steps.text: Light passes through the cornea, which does most of the bending
It crosses the aqueous humour and the pupil, which the iris sizes to the brightness
The lens fine-tunes focus: for near objects the ciliary muscle contracts and the lens rounds up
Light crosses the vitreous and lands on the retina, sharpest at the fovea
Rods and cones turn it into signals that travel along the optic nerve to the brain
